content.text:
Investigation complete. Findings:

- **No MFN/pricing-parity language anywhere**: searches for "most favoured/favored nation", "no less favourable", "parity", "best price", "lowest price", "match any", "competing offer", and "preferential" all returned nothing.
- **§ 11 (Fees)** is a bare payment obligation referencing Schedule "A" — no obligation for us to extend Garman terms given to third parties.
- **§ 10 / Page 5 (Maintenance)** contains only Garman-side service obligations and limited chargeable-repair carve-outs; no uplift tied to third-party pricing.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** and third-party references (§ 3(f), § 14, assignment) are unrelated to pricing parity.

Since no MFN obligation runs against Sparkling, the preferred position ("No MFN obligation on Customer") is already satisfied. An MFN in our favour would be welcome but its absence is not a burden to flag under this direction rule, so no redline is appropriate.

input.quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or pricing-parity provision in either direction. Section 11 (Fees) simply requires Sparkling to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule, and Section 10 / Page 5 (Maintenance and Support) impose service obligations on Garman with limited chargeable-repair exceptions at Garman's Fee Schedule rates; neither requires Sparkling to offer Garman terms no less favourable than those given to any third party or to match third-party offers. Targeted searches for "most favoured/favored nation", "no less favourable", "parity", "best price", "lowest price", "match any", "competing offer" and "preferential" returned no results, and the general provisions (Section 20) and other third-party references (Sections 3(f), 14 and the assignment clause) are unrelated to pricing. The preferred position of no MFN obligation burdening the Customer is therefore met; an MFN in our favour would be welcome but its absence is not a burden on us, so per the detection guidance no redline is proposed.
